NRL Casualty Ward: Fresh Reynolds injury; Ramien's season over
Broncos veteran Adam Reynolds faces a battle to return to the field before hanging up the boots after suffering a calf strain at training on Wednesday.
The premiership winner has not played since suffering a head knock in the Round 22 loss to the Knights and the latest setback puts his hopes of playing out his final season before retiring at the end of the year at risk.
In a statement, the Broncos said Reynolds will be assessed on a weekly basis to determine a return to play.
"Scans at the Clive Berghofer Centre’s Qscan facility confirmed that Broncos captain Adam Reynolds sustained a grade 1 soleus strain on his right calf at training yesterday," the club said.
"His return-to-play timeline will be determined on a week-by-week basis."
Cronulla centre Jesse Ramien has also played his final game for the club with the centre undergoing season-ending pectoral surgery on Thursday.
Ramien suffered the injury in the second half of last week's loss to St George Illawarra and will depart the Sharks at the end of the season to join the Cowboys.
"A big blow for the Sharks with Jesse Ramien ruled out for the remainder of the 2026 season after undergoing pectoral repair surgery today," the club said in a statement.
"The star centre hurt himself in the second half against the Dragons on Sunday afternoon; he then went for scans on Monday, but after seeing a specialist, it was decided the best course of action was surgery."

August 13 th 2026, 3:15pm , By: Ben Bridge
Saturday evening at CommBank Stadium brings together a Cowboys side clinging to a finals position and a Parramatta team with nothing to lose. North Queensland absolutely needs the two competition points and should win this game, but Cowboys -6.5 asks them to win by more than I am comfortable laying given the matchup history and their inconsistent recent form.
My fair spread is closer to Cowboys -3.5, making Eels +6.5 the play. It is only a small position because Parramatta have been impossible to trust all season, but they have repeatedly troubled North Queensland and have won five of the past six meetings between the sides. The Cowboys have also won just once in five visits to CommBank Stadium.
Parramatta lose Isaiah Iongi for the season after the fullback suffered MCL and PCL damage against South Sydney. Apa Twidle takes over at No.1, Dylan Walker returns on the bench and Junior Paulo starts in the front row. North Queensland name Scott Drinkwater at fullback, Jake Clifford and Jaxon Purdue in the halves and a powerful forward pack featuring Jason Taumalolo, Reuben Cotter, Griffin Neame and Reed Mahoney.
Eels vs Cowboys Prediction & Tips: 2026 NRL Round 24
Eels Show Fight After Horror First Half
Parramatta’s 28-24 loss to South Sydney was about as strange a performance as you will see. The Eels were dreadful for 40 minutes, trailing 28-0 at halftime after being completely overwhelmed by South Sydney’s attack. Brian Kelly spent time in the sin bin, Parramatta missed 29 tackles in the opening half and looked capable of conceding 50.
Then they nearly produced the biggest comeback in premiership history.
Parramatta scored 24 unanswered points after halftime and gave themselves a genuine opportunity to steal the game. Jordan Samrani’s acrobatic try reduced the margin to four with 13 minutes remaining, and the Eels suddenly looked like the side playing with greater energy and confidence. They eventually ran out of time, but the response at least showed this team has not completely checked out.
The cost was Iongi’s knee injury, which has ended his season. That removes one of Parramatta’s better attacking players from the backfield, with young Apa Twidle now asked to take over. Mitchell Moses remains the key to everything. If he can control field position and keep the Cowboys starting sets deep, Parramatta can make this ugly enough to stay inside the number.
The forward pack also looks competitive. Paulo starts alongside Luca Moretti, Jack de Belin provides experience at lock and Dylan Walker returns through the interchange.
This is still a bottom 4 team, but their best performances have generally come when opposition sides expect an easy afternoon. North Queensland cannot afford to treat them as one.
Cowboys Produce Massive Defensive Response
North Queensland’s 30-8 win over the Titans was exactly the response Todd Payten needed after the Cowboys had conceded 82 points to the Roosters one week earlier. Rather than trying to immediately repair their points differential through reckless attack, the Cowboys based the win on defence and repeatedly turned Gold Coast away despite the Titans receiving opportunities.
That response deserves enormous credit. North Queensland remains inside the eight and, importantly, their run home is favourable. Their remaining opponents sit below them on the ladder, meaning there are no excuses if they do not qualify for September.
The Cowboys still have some unusual selection features. Jaxon Purdue remains at halfback alongside Jake Clifford, while Scott Drinkwater is the primary attacking threat from fullback. Without Tom Dearden, they lack some of the direct running and composure that normally makes their spine dangerous.

August 14 th 2026, 1:13am , By: Scooby
The final game on NRL Super Saturday heads to Brisbane this week with the Broncos hosting the Warriors . Playing for pride, the Broncos will want to avoid conceding this contest as the Warriors look to consolidate their spot inside the Top 4. This sets the stage for an intriguing match. The intensity inside this stadium will only add to the spectacle and Before You Bet is here assist with a comprehensive look at what is ahead in this contest.
Also, Before You Bet will be providing free previews and betting tips for EVERY game in the 2026 NRL season, so make sure to head over to our NRL Tips regularly to keep up to date with all of our free content.
Broncos vs Warriors Predictions & Tips: NRL Round 24 2026
A team of two halves
Fans would’ve hope that the Broncos could repeat their first half effort against the Dolphins in Round 23 which saw them score 5 tries in thrilling fashion. That was short-lived though, as the Dolphins powered home to prevail 40-32 against a blundering Broncos outfit. With just 46% possession and a 79% completion rate, they couldn’t turn their 9.6m per carry into more points. While they set a strong platform in attack, they were loose defensively, allowing 7 line breaks and missing 27 tackles. Ultimately, the power of their opponents was too much. In previous years, this could’ve been a game they closed out but this is further evidence of their decline.
Making a statement
Welcoming the table-toping Panthers to Auckland, the Warriors needed to make a statement with a strong performance. They did just that as they powered their way to a comprehensive 28-12 victory. Leading 18-nil at HT, they continued their dominance in the second half. They controlled the speed of the game with 53% possession and an 83% completion rate, which allowed them to run for 9.9m per carry, make 624 PCM’s, and create 8 line breaks. Despite missing 35 tackles, they scrambled well defensively. This is another chance for them to prove how far they have come in a tricky road match.
Stats that matter
- These two sides met in Round 11 where the Warriors were victorious 42-12. The home team has won 8 out of the past 9 games played.
- The past 5 games between these two sides has seen blowout victories. The average winning margin is 18.4 points. They have been relatively low scoring matches, with the average total points sitting at 46.4.
- Given their struggles this season, it is no surprise to see the Broncos trail the Warriors on both sides of the ball. The home team averages just 18ppg in attack while conceding 27ppg defensively. The Warriors allow just 16ppg while scoring 28ppg.
Quality and execution to determine the winner
The Broncos have been flattered with the odds that are posted, and the value immediately rests with the Warriors. Their performance last week highlights their capabilities, and the Broncos have proven at several points this season that they are lacking consistency. There is no doubt that they will be motivated ahead of this contest but the relentless pressure the Warriors build in their play should expose the lack of maturity the Broncos possess.
Look for the Warriors to generate momentum in the middle of the field first, allowing their crafty outside backs to pressure the Broncos on the edge. This has been an issue for the home side throughout 2026 and while capable enough, consistency still eludes them. Once the Warriors gather enough momentum, they should pull away from their opponents to comfortably cover the line and consolidate their position in the Top 4 on the competition ladder.

Sunday afternoon at McDonald Jones Stadium looks like one of the clearest favourite spots on the NRL Round 24 card. The Knights are firmly entrenched in the finals race, return home after another huge victory in Canberra and now regain Bradman Best and Phoenix Crossland. Gold Coast , meanwhile, were poor last weekend and will continue to struggle without the organising influence they had received from young halfback Zane Harrison.
The current spread of Knights -13.5 is large, but I am happy to lay it. Newcastle already belted Gold Coast 36-12 during Magic Round earlier this season, and their attacking lineup now looks close to full strength. The Knights have won 12 games and remain in the top six, while the Titans sit near the bottom and have little beyond pride to play for.
Harrison is not available, with Lachlan Ilias retained at halfback alongside Jayden Campbell. Newcastle regains Best and Crossland after both missed the Canberra win with calf issues, while Kalyn Ponga, Dominic Young, Dane Gagai, Greg Marzhew and Fletcher Sharpe all remain in the backline.
The primary bet is Newcastle -13.5, but alternate spreads are absolutely on the table if the Knights begin strongly.
Knights vs Titans Prediction & Tips: 2026 NRL Round 24
Knights Keep Finding Ways to Win
Newcastle’s 30-24 victory over Canberra at GIO Stadium was another significant step in what has become one of the season’s great turnarounds. The Knights were pushed throughout and completed at only 66 per cent in the first half, but their strike players continually produced when the game demanded it. Dominic Young finished with 203 metres, 11 tackle breaks and two tries, while Francis Manuleleua ran for 153 metres with 11 tackle breaks of his own.
Kalyn Ponga was involved everywhere. He scored after backing up a 60-metre movement with Gagai and Young and repeatedly threatened Canberra despite making several errors under difficult conditions. The key difference was Newcastle’s ability to produce high quality attacking moments even when their overall execution was imperfect.
The win pushed the Knights to sixth and continued an extraordinary revival after finishing last in 2025. A win here keeps them right in the hunt for a top 4 spot come seasons end.
This week they become stronger again. Best returns in the centres, giving Newcastle another elite yardage carrier and attacking weapon on the left edge. Crossland resumes at hooker, providing far more experience around the ruck than Newcastle had last week.
The only notable fresh loss is Brodie Jones, who suffered a hamstring injury against Canberra. Tyson Frizell remains available from the bench, allowing Justin Holbrook to maintain plenty of experience through the middle despite a youthful starting pack.
